name: Leopard complex (appaloosa)
summary: The leopard complex (TRPM1), caused by a 1,378 base-pair retroviral insertion in intron 1 of the gene. Incompletely dominant for the coat, and two copies also cause night blindness and raise the risk of recurrent uveitis. What it shows depends on two other loci. LP alone gives the appaloosa characteristics - roaning that spares the bony parts, a scatter of white spots, striped hooves, a white-rimmed eye. The bold patterns - leopard, fewspot, blanket, snowcap - come from the PATN1 and PATN2 modifiers, which do nothing at all on a horse without LP. Found in the Appaloosa, Knabstrupper, Noriker and related spotted breeds. More than PATN1 modifies the pattern - further modifiers and polygenic background - but no second modifier has been identified, which is what the abstracted PATN2 stands in for.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: No leopard complex - a solid-coloured coat.

phenotypes.name: Mottled (LP characteristics)
phenotypes.description: One leopard-complex copy and no pattern modifier: light, uneven roaning that keeps its colour over the cheekbones, shoulders, hips and knees, a scatter of small white spots, striped hooves and a white-rimmed eye. The appaloosa “look” without a bold pattern.

phenotypes.name: Varnish roan
phenotypes.description: Two leopard-complex copies and no modifier: heavy, uneven whitening that leaves darker “varnish marks” over the horse's bones - cheekbones, shoulder blades, elbows, hips, stifles and knees - so it ends up outlined by its own anatomy. Not true roan and not a stronger version of it: patchy where classic roan is even, and it whitens the head, which classic roan never does.

phenotypes.name: Leopard
phenotypes.description: One leopard-complex copy plus PATN1: a white or cream body carrying round dark spots of the base colour, fairly evenly spread from head to hoof.

phenotypes.name: Fewspot leopard
phenotypes.description: Two leopard-complex copies plus PATN1: almost solid white, with only a handful of small spots left - usually on the flank, elbow and stifle.

phenotypes.name: Spotted blanket
phenotypes.description: One leopard-complex copy plus PATN2: a solid white sheet over the hips and croup with dark spots of the base colour inside it; the rest of the horse is its ordinary colour.

phenotypes.name: Snowcap blanket
phenotypes.description: Two leopard-complex copies plus PATN2: the same white blanket over the hips, with no spots in it at all.

phenotypes.name: Semi-leopard
phenotypes.description: A leopard-complex horse carrying both PATN1 and PATN2: a spotted white blanket that reaches well forward over the barrel, part-way to a full leopard.

conditions.name: Congenital stationary night blindness
conditions.description: Two leopard-complex copies. The horse sees poorly in the dark from birth - it does not get better or worse, and in daylight the horse is unaffected.

conditions.name: Equine recurrent uveitis risk
conditions.description: Two leopard-complex copies. A raised risk of equine recurrent uveitis, an inflammatory disease of the eye that can threaten sight.

interactions.note: The phenotype of this locus once the loci it depends on are known. Overrides the genotypes table.
